cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says Jehoiachin "…did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his father had done." (2 Kings 24:9). His father was Jehoiakim, the king before him (2 Kings 24:6). Three months on the throne, friends, and the writer still has that much to say about it.

The city comes under siege. The servants of Nebuchadnezzar marched up to Jerusalem, "…and the city came under siege." (2 Kings 24:10). A siege means the city gets surrounded and shut in. Nobody's popping out for errands, friends.

He surrenders to the king of Babylon. Jehoiachin, his mother, his servants, his commanders and his officials "…all surrendered to the king of Babylon." (2 Kings 24:12). Nebuchadnezzar had come to the city himself (2 Kings 24:11). I think that took some nerve of its own, handing it all over with the king right there.

The answer is False. The text says "Jehoiachin king of Judah, his mother, his servants, his commanders, and his officials all surrendered to the king of Babylon." (2 Kings 24:12). The whole group gave themselves up together, friends. Nobody stayed out of it.

The answer is False. Nebuchadnezzar "…carried off all the treasures from the house of the LORD and the royal palace…" (2 Kings 24:13). That covers the treasures in both places, bakers. None of them stayed put.

He cuts them into pieces. The text says Nebuchadnezzar "…cut into pieces all the gold articles that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD." (2 Kings 24:13). Those were made long before, in Solomon's day. That's a hard thing to read, friends, and I think it stings.

The answer is poorest. The text says "Only the poorest people of the land remained." (2 Kings 24:14). The commanders, the mighty men, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths were all taken, friends. The poorest were left behind in the land.

The answer is True. Nebuchadnezzar carried Jehoiachin to Babylon "…as well as the king’s mother, his wives, his officials, and the leading men of the land." (2 Kings 24:15). The wives are right there in the list, bakers. They were taken into exile too.

The answer is battle. The text says the seven thousand men of valor and the thousand craftsmen and metalsmiths were "…all strong and fit for battle." (2 Kings 24:16). These were the people you'd count on, friends. And Babylon took every one of them.

The answer is the king of Babylon. "…the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah." (2 Kings 24:17). Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, is the one who gets the job, bakers. And Babylon's king even gave him a new name, Zedekiah.
